problem:
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}{\int }_{z/x}^{x}8\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{4})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x=$

*Hint: Change the order of integration to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$*

activity_context.topic_title: Changing the Order of Integration in Triple Integrals: Changing Region

feedback.problem:
Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{{e}^{y}-1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $x,$ and then $z.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We wish to find limits of integration ${u}_{1}(y,z),$ ${u}_{2}(y,z),$ ${v}_{1}(z),$ ${v}_{2}(z),$ $a,$ and $b$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{{e}^{y}-1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡3,\,\,0\le x\le {e}^{y}-1}
$$

Now, let's sketch the region. Since it is a type II region, we first sketch the projection onto the $yz$-plane, given by

$$
E={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡3,\,\,0\le z\le 2}.
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14093829/assets/61d029135038017b000de51c15d8b392c0b80e98c49e78c8c82dfa79d6232878.png)

Then, the region $R$ is shown in the diagram below, where $0\le x\le {e}^{y}-1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14093829/assets/08a4f528a01415112e5b194617f0fc450a0a849060f08fe1959e0929ef366316.png)

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z,$ we write $R$ as a type III region and its projection $D$ onto the $xz$-plane as a type II *plane* region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $y$-axis and in the direction of increasing $y,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14093829/assets/4cd2d122764f82a6c38a9d657dcc579d2b93e676266604e03188ac933710dab0.png)

The arrow enters the region through the left boundary and leaves through the right boundary:

- The left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x,z),$ is

$$
x={e}^{y}-1\,⟹\,y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1).
$$

- The right boundary of the region is

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡3.
$$

Therefore, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡3},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14093829/assets/69b31f925d432360dc0796c3745782bacb6645bbabcf159f9049770c09359757.png)

We now consider the projection $D$ as a type II plane region in the $xz$-plane with the right curve given by 

$$
x={e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-1=2.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14093829/assets/dafed2ddc7ae18a05ec4fe1d5768f9b0f12456e0d2cf2552e91382d686d65522.png)

Hence, we have that

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 2}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $x,$ then $z,$ we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{{e}^{y}-1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.
$$
